archippus.title: Archippus
archippus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
archippus.note: Paul calls him a fellow soldier and tells him in public to finish the ministry he received in the Lord. He was at Colossae, likely part of Philemon's household.

aristarchus.title: Aristarchus
aristarchus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aristarchus.note: A Macedonian who travelled with Paul. He was dragged into the riot at Ephesus, sailed with Paul to Rome, and was imprisoned with him there.

barnabas.title: Barnabas
barnabas.about: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
barnabas.note: Joseph was his given name. He was a Levite from Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas, son of encouragement, after he sold a field and gave the money to the Jerusalem church.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

colosse.title: Colosse
colosse.note: Paul wrote Colossians to the church here, in Phrygia on the Lycus River near Laodicea and Hierapolis, without ever having visited. Epaphras, a local man, had brought the gospel. The mound is unexcavated, near modern Honaz in Turkey.

demas.title: Demas
demas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
demas.note: With Paul in his imprisonment, and then gone. Paul writes that Demas deserted him because he loved this present world.

epaphras.title: Epaphras
epaphras.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
epaphras.note: A Colossian who probably planted the church there and then brought Paul word of how it was doing, which is what set Colossians going. Paul says he was always wrestling in prayer for them.

gentile.title: Gentile
gentile.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gentile.note: Anyone who is not Jewish. The Greek word behind it means nation or people, and Paul's gospel turns on Gentiles being grafted into God's covenant people without first becoming Jews, the position defended at the Jerusalem council in Acts 15.

hierapolis.title: Hierapolis
hierapolis.note: In the Lycus Valley of Phrygia, alongside Colossae and Laodicea, and Epaphras worked hard for the church there. Its hot springs left white terraces that still draw people, at modern Pamukkale in Turkey. Early tradition says the apostle Philip died in the city.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

justus-2.title: Justus
justus-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
justus-2.note: Colossians names him once, and he is a man from the New Testament. The verse is Colossians 4:11.

laodicea.title: Laodicea
laodicea.note: A rich banking and cloth city in the Lycus Valley. It had no water of its own and piped it in from the hot springs at Hierapolis and the cold springs at Colossae, so it arrived lukewarm, and Revelation's "neither cold nor hot" plays on that. Its church gets the sharpest rebuke of the seven.

laodicean.title: Laodicean
laodicean.note: Someone from Laodicea, and Paul tells the Colossians to swap letters with the Laodicean church.

lucas.title: Lucas
lucas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
lucas.note: The Latin form of Luke, Paul's travelling companion and doctor. Early tradition gives him the Gospel of Luke and Acts, which would make him the one Gentile writer in the New Testament.

marcus.title: Marcus
marcus.about: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
marcus.note: John Mark. He set out with Paul and Barnabas and left partway through the first journey, and that later split the two men in a sharp quarrel. Peter calls him his son, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel of Mark from Peter's preaching.

nymphas.title: Nymphas
nymphas.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
nymphas.note: A church met in this believer's house, probably in or near Laodicea, and Paul sends greetings in Colossians 4:15. The manuscripts disagree on whether the name is Nymphas, a man, or Nympha, a woman.

onesimus.title: Onesimus
onesimus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
onesimus.note: A runaway slave who ended up with Paul in prison and became a Christian there. Paul sent him back to his owner. The letter to Philemon is Paul's request that Philemon take him in as a brother.

paul.title: Paul
paul.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul.note: Born Saul, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin and a Roman citizen from Tarsus. He trained as a Pharisee under Gamaliel and hunted the early church. Then the risen Christ met him in a blinding vision.

scythian.title: Scythian
scythian.note: Not a name but a people: nomads from the steppes north of the Black Sea and Caspian Sea, and the ancient byword for distant outsiders. Paul puts the Scythian in his list in Colossians 3:11.

timotheus.title: Timotheus
timotheus.note: Timothy, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. Paul took him along on his travels and trusted him with hard errands to churches in trouble, and two of Paul's letters are addressed to him.

tychicus.title: Tychicus
tychicus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tychicus.note: He carried Paul's letters, Ephesians and Colossians among them, and told the churches in person how Paul was doing.
